subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps

Hi John / Sara —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and immediate next steps from our demo:

1) Recap: we walked through the Redwood hosted endpoint for multi-turn support, prefix caching, and a short walkthrough of our eval dashboard. Your key constraints: 200ms median token latency goal for live chat, budget target ~$0.004/token effective, and high-fidelity entity extraction for downstream billing workflows.

2) Recommended immediate next steps:
  - We’ll share a post-demo shortlist of model variants tuned for latency/cost/quality tradeoffs (below).
  - We’ll push a small evaluation harness with your prompt set and 1k representative conversations. Expect link + results by Wed (05/05).
  - Set up a short pricing/contract touchpoint once you pick a preferred variant (Vivek to lead).

3) Attachments & links: recording attached (acme_demo_recording.mp4) and a preliminary eval workbook (redwood_model_evals_summary.xlsx). Full prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) is attached; running locally against the shortlist now.

Initial recommended shortlist (high-level rationale):
- Redwood-2.7Q (quantized): Best cost/latency balance for high throughput. Median token latency ~120-150ms on our standard Dedicated pool; expected cost ~0.0025/token with batching and prefix caching. Quality: high for conversational intent + structured extraction with modest prompt engineering. Good fit if you value throughput and cost.

- Redwood-7B-opt (optimized kernels): Stronger extraction accuracy, median token latency ~180-220ms; cost ~0.004/token. Recommended if extraction precision (billing line-items) is critical and you can accept slightly higher latency.

- LlamaX-13B (open model we benchmarked): Highest quality on entity recall at the cost of latency (~320-400ms) and cost (~0.007/token). Use for fallback/classification batch jobs where latency is not primary.

Why these three? They cover predictable tiers: fast+cheap, balanced, and high-precision fallback. We can route user-facing chat to Redwood-2.7Q with a canary fallback to Redwood-7B-opt for flagged examples, and async batch reprocessing with LlamaX-13B where you need max recall.

Next: I’ll share the eval links + raw results by Wed. Please reply if you want us to prioritize latency over cost (we can propose micro-quant / additional batching configs).

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. Couple quick clarifications before we run the eval: 

- For Redwood-2.7Q, can you confirm whether the 120-150ms median is measured at p95 concurrency (we expect traffic spikes to ~350 RPS)?
- For the Redwood-7B-opt, can you share the specific extraction metrics you mentioned (precision/recall on our sample billing entities)?

Also confirming we prefer low-latency for user-facing chat but need >95% entity recall for invoice parsing. If Redwood-2.7Q can meet recall with prompt templates you recommended, that’d be ideal. Otherwise we’ll consider the hybrid route you proposed.

—John

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps

Hey John — great questions. Short answers and links: 

- Latency baseline for Redwood-2.7Q: the 120-150ms median is measured on our Dedicated pool at steady-state with conservative batching (batch size 8); under p95 concurrency (~350 RPS) we see median shift to ~160-200ms and p95 around 420-480ms. We’ll include concurrency curves in the eval workbook (link below).

- Extraction metrics (sample run vs your prompt set): in our preliminary pass (attached workbook) Redwood-2.7Q achieved 92% entity recall / 94% precision after applying the suggested prompt templates (see prompt_examples section in the attached JSONL). Redwood-7B-opt achieved 97% recall / 96% precision on the same shard. LlamaX-13B led at 99% recall but with the latency/cost tradeoff noted.

Links: 
  - Preliminary eval workbook: https://redwood-internal/benchmarks/acme-2027-models (sheet: summary + concurrency curves)
  - Prompt set & templates: https://drive.google.com/acme_prompt_set_v1

Recommendation: start with Redwood-2.7Q in prod with the prompt templates we attached; configure an automatic sample-forwarding rule where low-confidence extractions (confidence < 0.8) are routed to Redwood-7B-opt for synchronous re-try up to a 250ms latency budget. For any post-hoc billing reconciliation jobs, run batch reprocessing on LlamaX-13B overnight.

I’ll sync with Vivek on pricing options for the dedicated pool (reserved vs burst) and tie it to the projected 350 RPS peak. Vivek — can you propose two pricing options (monthly reserved commit and a burst-capacity scenario) by EOD Wed?

Thanks — Marissa

Looping in quick pricing notes here so ACME has something to review: 

- Option A (Reserved Dedicated): commit 3x A100-equivalent slots for $25k/month — predictable latency, lower unit cost. Suggested if you want strict p95 targets and heavy daytime throughput.
- Option B (Burst + Hosted): baseline 1x reserved slot + burst pool + hosted fallback; estimated $12k/month baseline plus burst usage at host rates. Good if you want lower base commit while keeping headroom.

I’ll put formal quotes into HubSpot and attach a comparison sheet to the deal (ACME-2027-001). Marissa — I’ll also add the concurrency curves and the 1k eval results to the HubSpot deal record.
